newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK STABLE TO FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK STABLE TO FIRMER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted stable against the mark and the rand, but was firmer against the U.S. dollar and sterling at the close of fairly quiet trade on Friday, dealers said.
One dealer said market players were initially quoting higher exchange rates "for no apparent reason" before bringing them down again towards the close of business.
"The rates kept going up and down for no apparent reason -- there were no major payments or inflows (to warrant the movements)," he said.
The local unit finished the day at 11.1475/1575 against the U.S. dollar, up from Thursday's 11.1500/1600 and strengthened to 17.8800/9100 from 17.9700/9900 against sterling.
It closed largely unchanged at 6.5000/5200 against the mark from 6.5000/5100 and was also quoted steady at 2.4900/5200 versus the rand.
